How to choose RAM

Memory speed matters less than capacity for most desktop users. Sixteen gigabytes is a comfortable baseline for gaming and office work, while thirty-two gigabytes helps with video editing and virtual machines.

When you compare kits, look at the capacity first, then the generation your motherboard supports, and only then at frequency and latency. A well-priced kit with moderate timings usually beats an expensive one with a small advantage on paper.

Check that the kit is listed as compatible with your platform, and install two matching modules in the slots your manual recommends so that dual-channel mode is active.
